newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police widen probe into Briton's murder.
newsitem.headline: French police widen probe into Briton's murder.

text.p: French police are widening a probe into the murder of a British teenager two months ago to Switzerland and Italy after drawing a blank with other leads, sources close to the probe said on Wednesday.

Investigators travelled to Switzerland recently to do genetic tests on two pairs of motorcyclists who were staying in the youth hostel where 13-year-old Caroline Dickinson was sexually assaulted and killed on a school trip on July 18.
And they planned to visit Italy for similar tests on two motorcyclists living in Turin who were also staying that day in the youth hostel Pleines-Fougeres in Brittany, northwestern France.

Dickinson was found dead in her bed in a room she was sharing with four other girls. Genetic tests on teachers, youth hostel employees and her male classmates from Launceston Community College in Cornwall were negative.
The trips to Switzerland and Italy were to check on all those who had been in the hostel and were not prompted by active suspicions that any of them were involved, the sources said.

Police were also seeking to compare the crime with others committed in France for possible leads and were pinning most hopes on a search for a homeless man seen in the area around the time of the crime.
Frenchman Patrice Pade, arrested soon after the killing, was released after DNA genetic tests showed he could not have committed the rape. French police said he recanted a confession to the murder.
